newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Settlers lay claim to an Arab-owned Hebron land.
newsitem.headline: Settlers lay claim to an Arab-owned Hebron land.

text.p: Jewish settlers on Thursday began fencing off an Arab-owned hilltop near Hebron in a move that Palestinians said would fuel tension over the West Bank town, witnesses said.
They said about 30 settlers, mostly teenage students, hammered spikes around the sparsely planted hilltop near Kiryat Arba settlement and began encircling it with barbed wire.
The settlers briefly argued with Palestinian landowners before Israeli security forces separated the two sides and ordered the settlers to halt the work.
Israeli military authorities were not immediately available for comment.
"This is our homeland which we inherited from father to son. We have certificates to prove that this land belongs to us," said Ali Jaber, a 32-year-old landowner.
Hebron is the focus of Israeli-Palestinian talks on implementing a self-rule deal signed between the PLO and Israel in 1995. The U.S.-brokered talks are going on at Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba.

Under the accord, Israel was to have pulled out troops from most parts of Hebron in March and handed over powers to Palestinian police. The deployment was delayed by Islamic suicide bombings in Israel in February and March and was later put off by Israel's right-wing government, elected in May.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators are trying to reach an accord on implementing the redeployment while ensuring security for about 400 Jewish settlers living in the town.
About 130,000 Jewish settlers have taken up residence amid more than two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip since Israel seized the two territories in the 1967 Middle East war.
